key_insight: For pulmonary embolism risk stratification, medical records and cardiac biomarkers outperformed vascular imaging features, and even graph neural networks on vascular trees did not add predictive value.
clinical_relevance: In practice, missing blood tests may limit performance, but the study suggests that routine patient records plus available cardiac biomarkers may capture most of the useful risk signal.
method: Benchmarked tabular models using medical records and cardiac biomarkers.
Added vascular biomarkers extracted from CTPA to evaluate whether imaging-derived features improved prediction.
Tested graph neural networks on the vascular tree's intrinsic graph representation.
evidence_signal: The team evaluated a private cohort with complete data for PE risk stratification (n=353) and found that vascular features and vascular-graph models did not outperform strong tabular baselines.
watch_item: The dataset is small and private, so the finding that vascular graphs add little value should be validated externally before changing workflows.
paper_title: Pulmonary Embolism Risk Stratification from CTPA and Medical Records: Vascular Graphs Are Not All You Need
